newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 3.

text.p: The following are the top stories in the Irish press on Friday.

- Sinn Fein, the political party linked to the Irish Republican Army, has written to the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) inviting it to discuss electoral strategy for the next British general election.
- The government recorded a surplus of close to 300 million punts on its current budget last year, finance minister Ruairi Quinn will announce today.
- A sharp rise in consumer borrowing has increased the risk of a rise in interest rates.
- The very cold weather will continue over the weekend, a Met Eireann spokesman said.
- Interest rates could be on the way up again, because the economy is booming.
- Freezing fog caused chaos at Dublin airport as a dozen flights were either delayed or diverted.
- Chronic underfunding of university research could halt the hi-tech jobs boom, a confidential report says.
- The Irish Insurance Federation is increasing the level of commission paid to brokers for single premium pensions policies for 1997, it said yesterday.
